policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the affiliation as 'of the house of Caleb,' distinguishing the qere כָלִבִּי from the ketiv כלבו.
ASV names the woman 'Abigail,' matching the qere אֲבִיגַיִל rather than the ketiv אבוגיל; the alternative-rendering note concerns 'bottles' and does not bear on this unit.
ASV 'ready dressed' does not distinguish the qere עֲשׂוּיֹת from the ketiv עשוות, and the alternative-rendering note concerns 'bottles,' not this unit; the base qere therefore remains the fallback.
ASV addresses Abigail with 'thou hadst hasted and come,' selecting the second-person qere וַתָּבֹאת over the first-person ketiv ותבאתי.
